payload.title: mcp-server bctcExtractReconcileJob re-fires a 20-request batch every 30min with no pacing against pdf-extractor's single extraction slot — AC-3/AC-4 companions of FIX-PDFX-PEK-EXTRACT-202-ACCEPTED-THEN-SILENTLY-DROPPED-SEMAPHORE-1800S
payload.why_deferred: Fix lives in apps/mcp-server/ — outside apps/pdf-extractor/ (dev-pdf-extractor's zone_restricted boundary). Cannot be implemented by this agent.

evidence.ac3_answer: threading.Semaphore(1) in PekEngineAdapter was DELIBERATELY chosen (REQ-PEK-9d/AC-PEK-4d, docs/architecture-briefs/2026-05-26-pek-integrate-design.md §2.x: 'prevents two concurrent model instances from doubling RAM' against the Docker --memory 2.5g cap; measured +845.4 MiB RSS growth per single extraction per pek_engine_adapter.py's own FIX-PDFX-PARENT-PROCESS-MEMORY-BURST-HEADROOM comment). It was never a default value.
evidence.capacity_mismatch: 43 POST /pek-extract requests arrived in the 01Z hour on 2026-08-26 against 1 server-side slot. pek_engine_adapter.py's own comment names the caller: bctcExtractReconcileJob.ts (mcp-server) re-fires its whole still-pek_triggered batch (DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=20) every 30-min tick with no pacing.
evidence.which_side_should_change: The CALLER, not the server. Raising server concurrency risks the container's OOM-kill threshold (see ac3_answer). Raising PEK_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS was explicitly ruled out as a non-fix by PO on the origin row (po_ruling_20260826T0650Z).

payload.recommendation: File a P3 row for dev-mcp-server: give bctcExtractReconcileJob.ts either (a) a client-side market-hours gate (it currently burns pointless round-trips into the 02:00-07:59 UTC block window the guard already refuses), or (b) honor the detail.retry_after field the 503 response already carries, plus add inter-request/inter-batch pacing so a 20-request re-fire does not queue 19 requests behind pdf-extractor's single slot.
